title: The Tom Brown session and his demands
summary: Tom Brown's session was done at WDSU after rehearsals at the studio; he first wanted conditions but tore up his list after talking with Mares.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: The Tom Brown session, where was that done?
We did the Tom Brown session at WDSU also.
You usually had rehearsals over here though.

Yeah, we always put the session together here, we map out and we get our patterns here, who's going to play this and what's what, and go over the tunes, and exchange a few ideas. I have my own ideas what I want, but I always like to hear things and suggestions, and we always put them together and see, and as a rule, they always come out real nice. And Tom, like I said, we spoke a little further back on the tape, that Tom was very, very, I don't know exactly how to put it, but he wanted things right.

And he said he'd never record unless he got exactly what he wanted, and that's exactly what happened on the session I gave him. Like I told you earlier in the tape, when we played the tapes back, I says, Tom, what do you think of me? He says, exactly what I wanted.
I remember, I'm not trying to give any secrets right, but I think Eden had one of the agreements is the publicity and what went on, all the companies and everything. Oh yeah, he wanted,
he gave me a list of things that he wanted done.

But after we got talking and sat on and I pointed out to him this and thing, he told me, he said, you're right, Joe, I had a little heart on this thing and go ahead and do it the way you think it should be done. I'll leave it all in your hands and after that, we agreed that it was the right thing to do. And he was very satisfied and he tore up the papers of the little rules that he wanted. But I'll tell you why. Tom had done a little recording before and he wasn't satisfied. He was a side man but it seems like a couple of things that he did, I mean, the band wasn't up to par

at their best and they came out anyhow and Tom didn't like it which I don't blame Tom. When you're going to record, that's on there for keeps and for years to come and if you don't do it right, they'll say, well, who was Tom Brown? Listen to this. he couldn't play anything and so forth and all. But anyhow, I'm happy to say that he was very satisfied in my session and I was glad that I could give another good old fella a band of his own.
